business_rules: At most one live run per sensor id.
If the existing entry is an orphan (pid dead) the rejection does not apply — the orchestrator may reclaim and start fresh.
behavior.summary: Under the registry lock, the script looks up the live entry and short-circuits with a rejected Signal. No prepare, no spawn, no watcher.

description: Singleton invariant: a blocking sensor can have at most one live run. If /start-sensor finds an existing registry entry whose subprocess pid is alive, it refuses with verdict=fail metadata.kind=rejected and exits non-zero without spawning a new run.

evidence.rationale: Under the registry lock, runStart consults running_sensors.json and emits the rejected Signal when a live entry exists.

expected_outcome.summary: Stdout has one rejected Signal; exit code is non-zero; registry is unchanged.

name: Reject /start-sensor when sensor already has a live registry entry (singleton)

trigger.summary: Agent invokes /start-sensor on a sensor whose registry entry already exists and whose pid is alive.
